content:
maya: Heads-up — seeing a sudden wave of SSO lockouts affecting ~120 users across multiple regions; lots of rapid TZ flips in location history (US → SEA → EU) over ~10m. Alert from sec-bot at 2026-03-20T14:18Z.
andre: on it. can you paste the alert id and a sample user?
maya: alert id ALRT-9582. sample user: j.tan@redwood.com. session logs show fast geo jumps and repeated push sends.
sec-bot: Alert ALRT-9582: sso_lockout_wave. Affected tenants: redwood-dev, redwood-intake. Peak count: 118 at 14:16Z. Avg_geo_hop_count=2. MFA push rate x3 baseline.
olivia: MFA push spikes => possible push-fatigue bot or credential stuffing. Any IP patterns?
maya: logs: push_sent -> push_fail -> immediate new push from different IP within 20s.
samir: running quick correlation: `SigninLogs | where TimeGenerated > ago(30m) and AlertId=="ALRT-9582" | summarize count() by IP, ASN, Country`
andre: result: bulk from AS9123 (SEA hosting), many ephemeral IPs from same ASN.
olivia: suggest throttle push attempts and add temporary ASN denylist; notify support about user friction.
maya: containment plan: 1) throttle MFA pushes to 2 attempts per 5m; 2) revoke sessions older than 10m for flagged accounts; 3) add ASN denylist; 4) enable device checkpoint for new locations. I'll apply 1 & 3 in 5m.
sec-bot: Runbook sso-automated-lockout invoked. Recommended actions: throttle pushes, session revoke, escalate to incident if >500 users or data exfil suspected.
samir: doing dry-run revoke: `authctl revoke --filter "alert=ALRT-9582" --older-than 600 --dry-run` => 95 sessions would be revoked.
andre: go ahead with revoke. I'll push the throttle policy: `policyctl patch sso.thresholds --push-attempts=2 --window=300`.
ops-runbook-bot: policy change applied to policy sso.thresholds (version 3.7.2). Throttle active in prod.
maya: revoke executed. authctl returned 95 revoked, 2 failures (retrying).
olivia: pinging @support to prepare comms for impacted users. draft: "Temporary MFA throttling active to protect accounts; you may be asked to confirm device." 
support: got it. we'll send a notice to affected users and add a statuspage update if escalates.
samir: KMS check: `kms-audit --since 24h --filter service=auth` => no unusual KMS calls. No key access patterns outside normal.
maya: good, no KMS compromise. collecting logs into evidence bucket and saving to /evidence/incidents/ALRT-9582/
andre: metrics update: lockout rate dropped 78% after throttle; push attempts normalized. Geo-hop frequency reduced.
olivia: next steps: add permanent rule to deny ASNs with no business need, add automated detection for burst geo-hops, schedule post-incident review tomorrow 10:00AM.
maya: assigning postmortem owners: olivia (comm), samir (forensics), andre (policy follow-ups). I'll assemble timeline & artifacts.
sec-bot: Incident status: contained. Users affected: 118. Escalation not required. Create postmortem doc: /wiki/incidents/ALRT-9582
maya: thanks all. I'll close updates in 30m unless new anomalies appear.
